findings.title: Reference guard can delete an object whose approval is still uncommitted
findings.scenario: Complete a document or photo. After the independent cleanup enqueue commits and the object is written, delay the outer transaction before commit for more than five minutes. Run cleanup on another instance, then allow approval to commit.
findings.expected: Cleanup waits for the in-flight approval to resolve and preserves the object if approval commits.
findings.actual: The plain EXISTS query reads the previously committed asset, which references uploads/<id> rather than documents/<id> or media/<id>.jpg. It does not wait for the locked asset row. Cleanup deletes the object and marks DONE; the outer transaction can then commit APPROVED with a missing object.
findings.evidence: MediaService.java:199 and :209 independently enqueue cleanup five minutes ahead while complete holds the asset lock. Object writes occur at :202 and :210 before outer commit. MediaCleanup.java:97–99 checks only visible key references without locking; :106 deletes immediately. No transaction-wide deadline guarantees approval resolves within five minutes. This is a source-derived interleaving, not an executed integration reproduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate cleanup with the asset identified by the deterministic key. Acquire its lock nonblockingly before checking committed state, and defer cleanup when approval owns the lock. Define consistent lock ordering with cleanup-row upserts to avoid introducing a deadlock.
findings.repro_test: Use the proxied services and PostgreSQL. Pause approval after object write but before commit, advance the cleanup clock past five minutes, and invoke runDue concurrently. Verify cleanup defers; after commit the object remains, and after rollback it is eventually removed. Cover both sealed documents and public variants.

findings.title: Nested independent enqueue can exhaust the connection pool
findings.scenario: With the default pool size, synchronize ten completions for different assets so each holds its outer transaction connection before entering enqueueUnlessApproved.
findings.expected: Completion concurrency remains bounded without every request waiting for another connection held by the same request group.
findings.actual: Each REQUIRES_NEW call suspends an outer transaction that retains its connection and requests a second connection. With the pool occupied by the outer transactions, inner acquisition times out and otherwise valid completions fail.
findings.evidence: MediaService.complete starts its transaction and locks the asset at :126–128, then invokes enqueueUnlessApproved at :199 or :209. That method uses REQUIRES_NEW. application.yaml:12–13 sets a five-second connection acquisition timeout but supplies no pool sizing or completion admission control for nested transactions. Runtime reproduction was blocked by unavailable Java/Docker.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound concurrent completions while reserving connection capacity for independent enqueue transactions, or redesign durable intent creation to avoid nested connection acquisition. Size capacity explicitly for the chosen concurrency model.
findings.repro_test: Configure a two-connection pool, pause two distinct completions immediately before independent enqueue, then release both together. Assert successful bounded progress after the fix rather than connection acquisition timeouts.
